gloss: left-side component of a kanji; radical

definitions.gloss: left-side component of a kanji character
definitions.explanation: The structural component that appears on the left side of a kanji character. One of the major categories of kanji components used to classify and look up characters in dictionaries.

examples.japanese: この{漢字|かんじ}の{偏|へん}は{何|なん}ですか。
examples.english: What is the left-side radical of this kanji?

examples.japanese: 「{語|ご}」の{偏|へん}は{言偏|ごんべん}だ。
examples.english: The left-side component of the kanji for 'word' is the speech radical.

examples.japanese: {偏|へん}と{旁|つくり}を{組|く}み{合|あ}わせると{一|ひと}つの{漢字|かんじ}になる。
examples.english: When you combine a left component and a right component, you get a single kanji.

notes:
A term used in kanji study to refer to the left-side structural component of a character. In the traditional classification system, kanji components are categorized by their position within the character.

KANJI COMPONENT POSITIONS:
- {偏|へん}: left side (e.g., the {氵|さんずい} in {海|うみ})
- {旁|つくり}: right side (e.g., the {刂|りっとう} in {割|わ}る)
- {冠|かんむり}: top (e.g., the {宀|うかんむり} in {家|いえ})
- {脚|あし}: bottom (e.g., the {灬|れんが} in {点|てん})
- {構|かまえ}: enclosure (e.g., the {門|もんがまえ} in {間|あいだ})
- {垂|たれ}: top-left wrap (e.g., the {广|まだれ} in {店|みせ})
- {繞|にょう}: bottom-left wrap (e.g., the {辶|しんにょう} in {道|みち})

COMMON RADICALS CALLED {偏|へん}:
- {人偏|にんべん}: person
- {言偏|ごんべん}: speech
- {手偏|てへん}: hand
- {木偏|きへん}: tree
- {水偏|さんずい}: water
- {金偏|かねへん}: metal

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
Not to be confused with {変|へん} (strange) or {辺|へん} (area, vicinity), which have the same reading but completely different meanings.
